summary: Reserve a durable request ID for checkout and block another order after an uncertain outcome.
reason: A lost response after the server accepts an order must not cause a retry with a fresh ID and a second charge. Dry runs, rate limits, HTTP redirects, transport body replay, local history failures, and output failures must not bypass that rule.
validated_outcome: Synthetic command tests confirm pending outcomes take priority over token failures, dry runs expose only redacted previews without a reservation or token refresh, and an output failure leaves a confirmed receipt that blocks a second POST. Mock HTTP tests require one attempt for every write failure including 429 and write redirects, and verify writes have no replayable GetBody even with an Idempotency-Key header. Exact read-only order-history POST endpoints retain bounded 429 recovery. A reused-connection failure test warms a connection and then drops the response after one synthetic checkout POST, confirming that the transport does not replay it. Windows-specific tests exercise registry-backed reservations, locking across different USERPROFILE values, confirmed receipt acknowledgment, and fail-closed registry flush errors with cleanup of a pre-POST failed reservation, without calling the order provider. The Windows CI job runs those tests and builds the CLI.
